features.text: Patient has a history of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of the right breast.
Patient had a right breast lumpectomy on January 20th, 2020.
Patient has been feeling good since the lumpectomy and performs self-breast exams regularly.
Patient had a calcification in the right breast detected during a mammogram in October 2019.

Patient had an ultrasound of the right breast on November 3rd, 2019, which revealed a mass at the two o'clock position, 11 centimeters from the nipple in the retroareolar region, measuring 0.4 by 2 by 3 centimeters.
Patient had a polyp removed in 2018, which was not cancerous.
Patient had a tubal ligation after her last child.
Patient's mother had non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, and her father had prostate cancer and heart disease.
Patient has no family history of breast cancer.
Patient has no siblings and all children are healthy.
Patient has no history of smoking, illicit drug use, or heavy alcohol consumption.
Patient drinks socially and quit smoking about 30 years ago.
Patient is allergic to penicillin.
Patient had radiation therapy after the lumpectomy.
Patient decided against endocrine therapy after the lumpectomy.
Patient has high cholesterol and is working on exercise and diet to manage it without medication.
Patient has a history of back and knee pain, which is considered age-related.
Patient has no history of miscarriages or terminations.
Patient has five children, and they are all having children of their own.
Patient is post-menopausal and has not been on hormone replacement therapy.
Patient has skin thickening at the medial inferior aspect of the right breast, possibly due to radiation skin changes.
